label: Huawei OceanCyber 300 data security appliance
description: Huawei OceanCyber 300 - 2U data security appliance that detects and responds to ransomware across OceanStor Dorado, OceanStor hybrid flash, OceanStor Pacific and OceanProtect storage: one appliance manages up to 8 storage systems, detects at up to 50 TiB/hour across 23 billion files, and delivers air-gap policy, secure snapshots and orchestrated recovery. Hardware: 2x GE network ports, 1x iBMC management port and 2x 10/25GE optical ports.
notes: The hardware row is one line and it is a complete census: '**Port: GE network port x 2; iBMC network port x 1; 10/25GE optical port x 2**' - 2U, 447 mm wide. Two modelling decisions come straight out of that line. The **iBMC** port is out-of-band management (Huawei's IPMI), so it is declared as its own interface and kept **out of the LAN bridge group** - a lab that bridges it into the data network is wiring a management plane to the thing it is supposed to survive. And the **10/25GE optical ports** are 25G-capable cages carrying a 10G/25G ladder, not fixed 10G links. It is an **appliance, not a storage array**: it holds no user data, it inspects up to 8 connected storage systems at 50 TiB/hour and orchestrates their snapshots and recovery, so it carries `host` and `http-server` and no forwarding capability. 2U, mains powered, no PoE.
